title: Hybrid matching layer: close-enough phonetic word matching + sound-mode scoring (the core)
accept: Matching needs no audio: inputs are hypothesis strings (word and optional phone hypotheses) vs the expected sentence's WordTokens; outputs are typed MatchResults (exact, nearMiss, reject) plus which indices advanced.
Exact policy: hypothesis equal to target word (case/punctuation-insensitive) → accepted.

Close-enough policy: phoneme-level edit distance against the target's graphemePhonemeMap phonemes; accepted as NEAR-MISS when within threshold — at most 1 substituted phoneme for words <= 4 phonemes, at most 2 for longer words — thresholds read from the tuning file, never hardcoded (test asserts changing tuning constants changes behavior).
'gat' → 'cat' accepted as near-miss; 'dog' → 'cat' rejected (the PRD's canonical examples, as tests).
Near-miss results are distinguishable from exact results in the MatchResult type (drives wordAcceptedNearMiss and the §5 word_read correct/near_miss analytics distinction).

Hypothesis words that are not the current target are scored with lookahead 1: a hypothesis matching the NEXT word confirms (back-fills) the current one — both advance, current emitted as accepted before next (ordering test).
Self-corrections and repeats always accepted: a wrong attempt followed by a correct production accepts the word; repeating an already-accepted word never regresses state or double-advances (tests).
For hypotheses on the current word that match neither current nor next within threshold: no acceptance, result reject with the failed distance (feeds struggle detection in the tracker).

Sound mode (Units 14/15): sound_mode_scorer tracks a target phoneme sequence from phone-level hypotheses when the engine exposes them, weighting instances of the drilled/target phoneme most; where only word hypotheses are available it approximates by phonetic-distance scoring of those hypotheses against the phoneme sequence (both paths tested with scripted hypotheses); sound mode uses the separate looser threshold set from the tuning file with A-13 pinned defaults — accept when >= 60% of the target phoneme sequence is matched with per-phoneme distance <= 1, target-phoneme instances weighted double (tests assert the 60%/distance/double-weight policy exactly, and that changing tuning constants changes behavior).

Grapheme-to-phoneme for hypothesis words (needed to phonetically compare an arbitrary hypothesis like 'gat' that has no authored map): a small deterministic G2P for comparison purposes, unit-tested on the fixture vocabulary; documented as matcher-internal.
pinned_design: Unit 4 pinned (ratified, OQ-1): expected-text hybrid recognition, KidSpeak-style — the matcher always knows the target sentence; the engine is biased with expected words; hypotheses are scored against the known next word, never open-ended transcription. Match policy pinned: accept when hypothesis is the target OR phonetically close enough; closeness = phoneme-level edit distance against the word's graphemePhonemeMap phonemes; threshold at most 1 substituted phoneme for words <= 4 phonemes, at most 2 for longer (tunable constants in the Unit 6 tuning file). Near-miss acceptance is deliberately distinguishable (§5 analytics) and triggers the near-miss prompt path (Unit 6 governs the prompt; the matcher only classifies). Self-corrections and repeats always accepted; lookahead 1 with back-fill (hearing the next word confirms the current one). Word mode (stories) vs sound mode (twisters + Sound Garden echo: phoneme-sequence tracking, drilled/target phoneme weighted most, looser thresholds — A-13 pinned defaults: >= 60% of sequence matched at per-phoneme distance <= 1, target phoneme weighted double, tunable). v1 bar is the happy path: quiet room, one child, cooperative reading — noise/accents/cross-talk explicitly deferred post-POC.
notes: This is the product's core risk (R1) and the hardest pure-logic unit — hence intensive. Fully headless: no audio, only hypothesis strings. The comparison G2P for out-of-vocabulary hypotheses is matcher-internal machinery (the PRD pins phoneme-level edit distance but hypothesis words arrive as text); keep it minimal and deterministic, cover the test vocabulary, and document its limits — do NOT let it grow into a linguistics project. Sound-mode default thresholds are now pinned (A-13; former OD-1 resolved) — still read them from the tuning file, never hardcode. Sound mode serves both twister-flow (Unit 14) and sound-garden (Unit 15). Emission of tracker events is listening-tracker's job; this ticket returns MatchResults only. ORCHESTRATOR-PINNED DEFAULTS for behaviors the test suite deliberately leaves unasserted (recorded, tunable, owner-vetoable): (1) inter-phoneme distance is uniform — any substitution/insertion/deletion costs 1 (plain Levenshtein over phoneme ids); (2) [REVISED at listening-tracker integration, orchestrator-ruled against the original default after it contradicted the PRD's ratified lookahead back-fill text and the tracker's frozen fixture]: current-word exact always wins; current-word near-miss yields to next-word EXACT (back-fill both); next-word near-miss never outranks current-word near-miss; (3) distance-0 hypotheses with different spelling (homophones) grade as exact; (4) reject phonemeDistance aggregates as the MIN across hypothesis candidates; (5) 'repeats always accepted' reaches back only to the most-recently-accepted word, and near-miss-shaped repeats are likewise non-events; (6) sound-mode alignment is greedy in-order matching — out-of-order productions are ignored without penalty; (7) multi-word hypothesis candidates are whitespace-split into individual candidate tokens.
